title: [native_aot][7/7] build_stage2: relink, patch the wheel, and the build wiring
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #191669
* #190899
* #190898
* #190897
* __->__ #194243
* #194242
* #194241
* #194240
* #194239
* #194238
* #190896

Human note:

Finally putting everything together. Relink libtorch_cuda, correctly fixup the wheel, and
make sure everything (paths, manifests, etc.) are all aligned and correct.

Claude note:

The driver on top of the verdict, and the CI and dev flows that call it. With
this commit a standard CUDA build ships embedded AOT kernels.

A post-install step, because the kernel builders package-import torch and
scikit-build-core has no post-build hook inside the PEP 517 backend. It
reconfigures before a targeted relink of torch_cuda: the generated file registers
itself in CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS only from the reconfigure that first READS it,
and the build.ninja on disk predates this generation -- without that the relink
silently omitted the kernels (417 MiB where 423 ships).

--wheel patches the relinked library and its RECORD entry back into the built
wheel, so test jobs get the kernels rather than a library replaced only on disk;
released wheels get the same before repair_wheel.py, so it goes through patchelf
like any other. It asserts that torch imports, because a kernel-free release wheel
must fail rather than skip -- and the ASan and TSan images cannot `import torch`
plainly, which is why the CI call is CUDA-guarded.

It assumes the torch it finds installed is the one this tree just built, and
VERIFIES that rather than repairing it: the reconfigure has to report embedding
before anything is relinked, the relinked library has to report its own kernels
before this exits, and a failure past that point says to reinstall. A run that
DECLINES overwrites a native_aot.cmake an earlier one left behind, because the
include is unconditional and the release matrix shares one build tree across eight
interpreters -- so the wheel for an interpreter with no DSL runtime was shipping
the previous interpreter's objects.

caffe2/CMakeLists.txt gets the one include line, EnvVarForwarding.cmake caches
TORCH_NATIVE_AOT so the opt-out survives a reconfigure, and CONTRIBUTING.md states
the skip reasons.

Test Plan:

```
pytest tools/test/test_native_aot_tools.py
```

Run at this commit's own tree, in a checkout with no built torch -- which is
what lint.yml's "Test tools" job has. This commit's tests cover patch_wheel's
RECORD and its ZIP64 metadata -- a copied member must not inherit the source's
stale offsets, which pip and unzip accept and `uv` refuses -- each of main()'s
refusals from the verdict down to a relink that produced no library, the argv and
env contract with both children including the one artifacts directory they share,
and the CI shells and CMake read as text.

PR CI cannot reach the relink at this commit -- no declaration exists yet, so
should_run() reports "nothing declares kernels" in every build job -- so it was
exercised by hand on a clean tree:

```
rm -rf build && USE_CUDNN=1 USE_CUDA=1 USE_MSLK=1 MAX_JOBS=32 spin develop
```

Stage 2 exported all four declarations (54 objects + 4 generated sources, 4.0 MiB),
reconfigured, relinked, copied 324 MiB over the installed torch and passed its
embedded-kernel probe. On that build: test/python_native, one file per process, 331
passed; `test_ops.py -k "cuda and (topk or scatter_add or index_add)"` 115 passed;
test_sort_and_select 207; test_scatter_gather_ops 247; test_indexing 380.

Authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).
